papers.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
papers.key_finding: LLM agents with rich memory and reflection produce believable human behaviour in simulated environments

papers.title: Generative Agent Simulations of 1,000 People
papers.key_finding: Individual-level demographic + interview data enables 85% accuracy in predicting survey responses for 1000 real people

papers.title: Out of One, Many: Using Language Models to Simulate Human Samples
papers.key_finding: Conditioning LLMs on demographic backstories produces response distributions that closely match real human survey data ('silicon sampling')

papers.title: The Challenge of Using LLMs to Simulate Human Behavior
papers.key_finding: LLM personas exhibit systematic positive bias (~20-30% overstatement of acceptance) and homogeneity bias compared to real humans

papers.title: Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk
papers.key_finding: Losses are weighted approximately 2x more than equivalent gains in decision-making -- foundational for all price reaction simulations

papers.title: Mental Accounting and Consumer Choice
papers.key_finding: Consumers maintain mental accounts that affect how they perceive price changes -- a 10% increase on a 5 EUR item feels different from 10% on a 50 EUR item

papers.title: Vocal Minority and Silent Majority: How Do Online Ratings Reflect Population Perceptions of Quality
papers.key_finding: Online ratings systematically overrepresent extreme opinions. The silent majority (~95% of customers) holds more moderate views.

papers.title: Culture's Consequences: Comparing Values, Behaviors, Institutions and Organizations Across Nations
papers.key_finding: Six cultural dimensions (PDI, IDV, MAS, UAI, LTO, IVR) predict systematic differences in consumer behaviour across countries

papers.title: Diffusion of Innovations
papers.key_finding: Innovation adoption follows a predictable curve: innovators (2.5%), early adopters (13.5%), early majority (34%), late majority (34%), laggards (16%)

papers.title: Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In
papers.key_finding: Principled negotiation (interests over positions) and BATNA (best alternative) are the strongest predictors of negotiation outcomes

papers.title: LLM Generated Persona is a Promise with a Catch
papers.key_finding: LLM personas are sensitive to persona framing -- small prompt changes can flip predictions. Structured demographic anchoring is critical.

papers.title: How Far Are LLMs from Being Our Digital Twins? A Benchmark for Persona-Based Behavior Chain Simulation
papers.key_finding: LLMs achieve 0.52 accuracy simulating nonfiction personas -- significant room for improvement with structured data.

papers.title: Using Large Language Models to Simulate Multiple Humans and Replicate Human Subject Studies
papers.key_finding: LLMs can replicate classic social science experiments when properly conditioned with demographic and contextual information.

papers.title: Large Language Models Assume People Are More Rational Than We Really Are
papers.key_finding: LLMs overestimate human rationality in decisions. Must inject irrationality, habit, and emotion into persona prompts.

papers.title: Toward Accurate Psychological Simulations: Investigating LLMs Responses to Personality and Cultural Variables
papers.key_finding: LLMs struggle with accurate cultural simulation without explicit cultural context injection.

papers.title: Advances in Prospect Theory: Cumulative Representation of Uncertainty
papers.key_finding: Cumulative prospect theory -- people overweight small probabilities and underweight large ones.

papers.title: Who is the Fairest of Them All? An Attributional Approach to Price Fairness Perceptions
papers.key_finding: Price fairness depends on attributed cause -- cost-driven increases are 60% more accepted than profit-driven ones.

papers.title: Perceived Price Fairness and Dual Entitlement
papers.key_finding: Dual entitlement theory: customers feel entitled to a reference price, firms feel entitled to a reference profit. Violations trigger outrage.

papers.title: Voice, Exit, and Negative Word-of-Mouth Behaviors: An Investigation Across Three Service Categories
papers.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
papers.key_finding: Dissatisfied customers choose between voice (complain), exit (leave), or negative WOM. Most choose exit silently.

papers.title: A Meta-Analysis of Organizational Complaint Handling and Customer Responses
papers.key_finding: Effective complaint handling can increase loyalty above pre-failure levels (service recovery paradox). Speed of response is the strongest predictor.

papers.title: Online Review Solicitations Reduce Extremity Bias in Online Review Distributions
papers.key_finding: Unsolicited reviews are bimodally extreme. Solicited reviews reduce extremity by ~30% and better represent the true population.

papers.title: Anchoring, Information, Expertise, and Negotiation: New Insights from Meta-Analysis
papers.venue: Ohio State Journal on Dispute Resolution
papers.key_finding: Meta-analysis confirms first offer anchoring effect accounts for 30-50% of final negotiation outcome. Effect persists even for experts.

papers.title: Passive Innovation Resistance: The Curse of Innovation?
papers.key_finding: Most innovation resistance is passive (status quo preference) not active (evaluation-based rejection). ~60% of resistance is passive.

papers.title: Not All Repeat Customers Are the Same: Designing Effective Cross-Selling Promotion on the Basis of Attitudinal Loyalty
papers.key_finding: Behaviorally loyal (habitual) customers respond differently to promotions than attitudinally loyal ones. Must distinguish the two in simulations.

papers.title: An Integrative Framework for Customer Switching Behavior
papers.key_finding: Switching behavior is driven by: pricing (30%), service failure (25%), inconvenience (20%), competition (15%), involuntary (10%).
